title: Existentialism
examples: How is existentialism different from other philosophies?
What does 'existence before essence' really mean for a person?
Can we really be totally free, according to Sartre?

explain.say: Today we explore existentialism, a big idea about being human.
This means we are born first, and then we create who we are.
A concrete example is that of a person choosing a career path.
Next, we look at the idea of radical freedom and responsibility.
This means we are totally free to make choices, and we are responsible for everything.
Jean-Paul Sartre is the main philosopher connecting these ideas for us.

draw.text: Sartre: 'Man is condemned to be free'

faq.q: What does 'existence before essence' really mean?
faq.a: It means that humans are born into the world first, and only through our actions do we define what it means to be us.
asks: Does this mean I can be anything?
Is my life a blank page?

faq.q: If I am totally free, does that mean I can't fail?
faq.a: No, freedom means we are responsible for our choices, but making a mistake is part of the process of defining ourselves.
asks: Is there any limit to my freedom?

faq.q: What is Sartre's main argument about freedom?
faq.a: Sartre argued that we are radically free, meaning we cannot escape making choices, even when it is difficult.
asks: Does Sartre say we have to choose everything?

faq.q: Does this philosophy say we have a purpose?
faq.a: Existentialism suggests that we do not have a pre-set purpose; we must create our own meaning through living.
asks: Are we meant to do something specific?
Is there a divine plan for me?

faq.q: How does this apply to my daily life?
faq.a: It suggests that every decision, from small habits to big life goals, is an opportunity to define yourself.
asks: Should I worry about my choices?
What is the practical use of this idea?

facts: Existentialism emphasizes individual freedom and choice.
The core concept is that existence precedes essence.
Jean-Paul Sartre is a key figure in this philosophy.
Responsibility for one's choices is absolute in this view.

quiz.say: If existence precedes essence, what does this suggest about human nature?

options.show: We define ourselves through our actions.
options.say: We define ourselves through our actions.

options.show: We are born with a divine plan.
options.say: We are born with a divine plan.

options.show: Our actions are only influenced by our upbringing.
options.say: Our actions are only influenced by our upbringing.

quiz.why: This is correct because it means we are not born with a fixed purpose or nature.

wrong.1: This suggests a pre-determined nature, which contradicts the idea of freedom.
wrong.2: This limits freedom, ignoring the choices we make despite our environment.
wrong.3: This removes personal responsibility from the individual's choices.

quiz.say: According to existentialism, if you choose to study medicine, what are you doing?

options.show: The school will define your worth.
options.say: The school will define your worth.

options.show: You are creating an essence for yourself.
options.say: You are creating an essence for yourself.

options.show: You are fulfilling a pre-written role.
options.say: You are fulfilling a pre-written role.

quiz.why: This shows that the choice itself helps build who you believe you are.

wrong.0: This delegates the definition of self to an external authority.
wrong.2: This implies your role was already decided before you started.
wrong.3: This suggests that past circumstances limit all possible future choices.

quiz.say: If one accepts radical freedom, what must one accept?

options.show: Waiting for others to guide you.
options.say: Waiting for others to guide you.

quiz.why: Because we are free to choose, we must own the outcomes of those choices fully.

wrong.0: This implies that guidance is necessary to make a choice.
wrong.2: This is an attempt to escape the weight of personal choice.
wrong.3: Existentialism rejects excuses for actions taken.
